item.title: Airtel Mulls UK Listing of its Money Unit in Dollars
item.description: Airtel Africa Plc is considering having its mobile payments arm trade in US dollars when it lists it in London later this year, an arrangement that’s only been seen a handful of times.

item.title: Oil Spills Show Cost of Keeping Middle East Barrels Flowing
item.description: As producers keep crude moving during the war, leaks across the Gulf are exposing the growing environmental toll.

item.title: Partners Group Becomes Worst Performer Among Europe Financials
item.description: Partners Group Holding AG became the worst performing stock in MSCI’s sector index for European financial companies this year, signaling investor concern over redemptions from its popular evergreen funds.

item.title: Amazon Delivery System Under Pressure From New York City Proposal
item.description: A city council proposal calls for Amazon to hire its contract delivery couriers

item.title: US saving slump nears record low in challenge to spending
item.description: If the rate hits 0%, question is whether Americans leverage up or sell assets.

item.title: Copper Crunch Worsens as Key Spread Heads for Highest Since 2021
item.description: Spot copper prices are surging above later-dated futures on the London Metal Exchange, in a condition known as backwardation that’s a hallmark of a deepening squeeze on supply.

item.title: Ukraine Says Black Sea Port Closures May Halve Farm Exports
item.description: Ukraine said it may halve its intended agricultural exports as the country’s remaining Black Sea ports in the Greater Odesa area are effectively shut amid Russian airstrikes, posing risks to the global food supply.

item.title: AI Drove Growth at Indeed After Investors Feared the Worst for Jobs-Search Site
item.description: AI sparked growth at a jobs-search platform that some investors feared doomed.

item.title: Boeing Analysts Turn Most Bullish Since 2022 on ‘Momentum Shift’
item.description: Boeing Co.’s efforts to turn around its business are getting a loud cheer from Wall Street, as analysts this week turned the most bullish on the company in nearly four years.

item.title: Zambia Electoral Body Suspends Vote Counting, Cites Violence
item.description: Zambia’s electoral commission halted vote counting in the southern African nation’s general election, citing reports of violence, as the main challenger to President Hakainde Hichilema warned against delaying the release of the results.

item.title: Dangote Sugar Raises $356 Million in Share Sale to Trim Debt
item.description: A sugar refinery owned by Africa’s richest person, Aliko Dangote, raised $356 million in a share sale and will use the funds to reduce debt and boost a capital position eroded by three years of losses.

item.title: Petrochemicals Maker Braskem Beats Estimates Amid Cash Woes
item.description: Braskem SA reported better-than-expected results in the second quarter, benefitting from war-related disruptions to petrochemical supplies from the Persian Gulf and Asia.

item.title: India Steps Up Review of Closing Stock Auction as Concerns Mount
item.description: India’s market regulator has accelerated discussions with high-frequency trading firms and other market players, people familiar with the matter said, on growing concerns over its new auction system to determine stock closing prices.

item.title: Bessent Gets a Warning on Deficits From the Bond Market
item.description: Auction results in highest 30-year yield since 2001.

item.title: Lagarde’s WEF Trip Set to Revive Talk of Early ECB Exit
item.description: Christine Lagarde will speak at the World Economic Forum’s headquarters in Geneva next week, a visit that’s likely to revive discussions about an early departure as European Central Bank president.

item.title: Beaten-Down Ocado Shares Show Signs of Revival with 45% Rally
item.description: Once a market standout, Ocado Group Plc shares are showing signs of life again after a bruising decline.

item.title: Iranians Struggle to Afford Groceries as Trump Squeezes Economy
item.description: In a little over a decade since starting her business in Tehran, Nazanine has weathered US sanctions, successive currency collapses and two wars. This is the first time she’s had to use credit to buy groceries.

item.title: Slovak Factories Are Losing Competitiveness, Central Bank Warns
item.description: Slovakia’s industrial sector, the backbone of the country’s economy, is losing competitiveness as productivity stagnates and labor costs surge by more than twice the European Union average, according to the country’s central bank.

item.title: Amazon, Michaels Benefit as More Americans Spend on Crafts And Hobbies
item.description: Pastime categories as a share of US goods consumption is at a record, beating pandemic highs

item.title: Putin Is Ready to Meet Witkoff, Kushner Again, Lavrov Says
item.description: President Vladimir Putin is ready to meet US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Russia to discuss Ukraine, though it matters what proposals they bring, Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said.

item.title: Prabowo Plans Indonesian Commodity Exchange to Control Prices
item.description: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto said the country would open a new commodity exchange in an effort to exert more influence on world commodity prices.

item.title: BofA’s Hartnett Sees a Republican Senate Win Fueling Stock Rally
item.description: Success in the midterm elections for the Republicans and the Texas gubernatorial contest would set up stocks for a further rally, according to Bank of America Corp. strategists.

item.title: China Aid for Key Sectors Can Feed Trade Tensions, ECB Blog Says
item.description: Chinese subsidies for strategic industries are boosting exports in those areas, according to European Central Bank research that adds to an intensifying debate among the region’s policymakers about such practices.

item.title: China’s Credit Growth Exceeds Forecasts Despite Rare Loan Slump
item.description: China’s credit expansion held up better than expected in July, but weak borrowing demand among households and businesses pushed loans into a worse-than-forecast contraction.

item.title: Hong Kong Raises Growth Outlook as Global AI Demand Boosts Trade
item.description: Hong Kong raised its full-year growth forecast after a global investment boom in artificial intelligence supercharged exports and helped deliver the economy’s strongest first-half performance in almost five years.

item.title: Kioxia Buyback Propels Japan’s Corporate Stock Buying to Record
item.description: Japanese corporations logged the highest weekly equity purchases on record as memory maker Kioxia Holdings Corp.’s share buyback bolstered the tally.

item.title: Taiwan Predicts First Year of Double-Digit GDP Growth Since 2010
item.description: Taiwan raised its growth forecast for the year to more than 10%, on track for the first double-digit increase since 2010, as the economy of the chip hub outperforms on AI.

item.title: Rupee Swings Fizzle Out as India’s Central Bank Tightens Grip
item.description: India’s central bank, whose programs are drawing in billions of dollars of overseas cash, is increasingly present in foreign-exchange markets to tamp down rupee volatility, offering a more predictable trajectory for the Asian currency.

item.title: Providence Agrees to Buy UK Property Valuation Provider Hometrack
item.description: Providence Equity Partners has agreed to acquire property valuation service Hometrack, people familiar with matter said.

item.description: Is this the big one?
